name: The q-value (as shipped)
text: The q-value (as shipped). Assumption: Storey's estimate of the share of true nulls assumes null p-values uniform on (0, 1); the route adjusts only the terms with at least one list protein, which breaks that assumption for small sets. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.7 % to 42.9 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 44.8 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 10 of 18 settings, failed in 6 (E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, no parent terms: lower limit 15.1 %; E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, parent terms: lower limit 19.9 %; E. coli full proteome, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 13.3 %; E. coli 2,000-protein subset, lists of 25, parent terms: lower limit 14.0 %; yeast, lists of 25, no parent terms: lower limit 8.0 %; yeast, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 39.2 %) and was not determined in 2. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 23.6 % (yeast, lists of 126, no parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.2 % to 35.7 % (highest upper limit 38.7 %; controlled in 15 of 18 settings, failed in 3 (E. coli full proteome, small planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 7.5 %; yeast, small planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 29.5 %; yeast, mid planted process, lists of 126, no parent terms: lower limit 18.2 %), not determined in 0), the planted term called in 80.5 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested, and against Benjamini-Hochberg over the same terms it called the planted term at most 3.8 % more often (paired; highest one-sided lower limit over 18 settings 0.0 %; a material gain needs 5.0 %).
added_after_scoring: [computed after scoring, reported; not the declared text; how obtained: results.md section 5] Against the default (Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family) it called the planted term up to 5.8 points more often with parent terms (E. coli 2,000-protein subset, small process: 23 more of 400 lists, none fewer) and up to 8.8 points more often without (yeast, large process), a gain that comes with the failures above. On planted lists of 25 with parent terms (E. coli, mid-size process; reported, not deciding) its mean false discovery proportion was 10.7 % (95 % interval 8.5 % to 12.9 %).

name: Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein
text: Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein. Assumption: Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein; that family is selected on the p-value (p below 1), for which Benjamini-Hochberg has no general guarantee. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.6 % to 8.2 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 9.3 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 16 of 18 settings, failed in 0 and was not determined in 2. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 0.5 % (E. coli full proteome, lists of 25, parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.2 % to 2.6 % (highest upper limit 3.8 %; controlled in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0, not determined in 0), the planted term called in 78.5 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested.
added_after_scoring: [computed after scoring, reported; not the declared text; how obtained: results.md section 5; appended if it is offered] In 2 of the 18 random-list settings (lists of 25 without parent terms: E. coli full proteome 7.2 %, yeast 8.2 %) it exceeded its nominal 5 % (lower limits 5.4 % and 6.3 % after Bonferroni adjustment over the 108 classifications; observed after scoring, not a declared classification).

name: Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family
text: Benjamini-Hochberg over the whole size-filtered family. Assumption: Benjamini-Hochberg over every term of 10 to 500 proteins; its guarantee needs independent or positively dependent tests, which overlapping Gene Ontology sets do not ensure. On random protein lists (no true signal; 18 settings: E. coli full proteome and a 2,000-protein subset, yeast; lists of 25, 126 and 400 proteins; with and without parent terms), 1.0 % to 2.5 % of lists had at least one significant term (highest one-sided 95 % upper limit 3.1 %; line 7.5 %): it controlled false calls in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0 and was not determined in 0. Lists with 10 or more significant terms: at most 0.1 % (E. coli 2,000-protein subset, lists of 25, parent terms). On lists of 126 with one planted process, mean false discovery proportion 0.1 % to 1.7 % (highest upper limit 2.7 %; controlled in 18 of 18 settings, failed in 0, not determined in 0), the planted term called in 74.8 % to 100.0 % of lists where it was tested.
added_after_scoring: [computed after scoring, reported; not the declared text; how obtained: results.md section 5] Against the q-value as shipped it called the planted term up to 5.8 points less often with parent terms and up to 8.8 points less often without, and against Benjamini-Hochberg over the terms with at least one list protein up to 3.8 and 5.1 points less often; never more often.
